{"content": "## Creating a Google Cloud Compute Engine Instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

Below are two ways to create the instance:

1. **Using the `gcloud` CLI** (recommended for most users).
2. **Using the REST API** (for programmatic automation or integration with other tools).

Both examples assume you have already:
- Enabled the **Compute Engine API**.
- Set up a **Google Cloud project** and **billing**.
- Installed the **Google Cloud SDK** and authenticated with `gcloud auth login`.
- Created a **service account** with the necessary scopes if you plan to use the REST API.

---

### 1. `gcloud` CLI Command

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # choose a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true,enable-oslogin=true \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --network-interface=network-tier=PREMIUM,subnet=default
```

**Explanation of key flags**:
- `--accelerator`: Adds the RTX A6000 GPU.
- `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true`: Triggers the automatic installation of the NVIDIA driver after the instance boots.
- `--scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`: Grants full access to Cloud APIs (adjust if you need tighter scopes).
- `--tags=http-server,https-server`: Allows HTTP/HTTPS traffic via the default firewall rules.

After the instance starts, the NVIDIA driver will be installed automatically. You can SSH into the instance and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh $INSTANCE_NAME@$PROJECT_ID.$ZONE.c.$PROJECT_ID.internal
nvidia-smi
```

---

### 2. REST API Call

**Endpoint**:
```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

**Request Body** (JSON):
```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {"key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true"},
      {"key": "enable-oslogin", "value": "TRUE"}
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Authentication**:
- Use OAuth 2.0 with a bearer token that has the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.
- Example using `curl`:

```bash
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the request body.

---

### Post‑Creation Steps
1. **Verify GPU**:
   ```bash
   gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a --command="nvidia-smi"
   ```
2. **Install CUDA Toolkit (if needed)**:
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-cuda-toolkit
   ```
3. **Configure Firewall** (if you need custom ports):
   ```bash
   gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-custom-ports \
     --allow tcp:5000-6000,udp:5000-6000 \
     --target-tags=http-server,https-server \
     --description="Allow custom ports"
   ```

---

**Tip**: If you plan to run GPU workloads frequently, consider using a **preemptible** instance or a **custom machine type** to reduce costs. Just adjust the `--preemptible` flag or the `machineType` field accordingly.

---

**Resources**:
- [Google Cloud Compute Engine Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs)
- [NVIDIA GPU Driver Installation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/install-drivers-accelerator)
- [REST API Reference](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/instances/insert)

---

Feel free to adapt the parameters (zone, machine type, disk size, etc.) to fit your workload and budget.", "filename": "create-rtx-a6000-instance.md"}
